lenses.failure_description: The optional punctuation style is under-specified, so different readers form different assumptions about what counts as punctuation style, when it applies, and which greeting outputs it should affect.
lenses.observable_signal: Two reasonable implementers describe different expected outputs for the same input or ask clarifying questions about scope, defaults, or allowed styles.
lenses.why_material: If the ambiguity is not surfaced early, the handoff cannot be implemented consistently and downstream work will diverge.
lenses.minimal_test_shape: Give two people the same seed and ask each to write three example greeting outputs for default and optional cases; compare for mismatches.

lenses.failure_description: The optional nature of the punctuation style is not expressed in a way that makes the user's selection or non-selection externally clear at the interface boundary.
lenses.observable_signal: Observers cannot tell from the request or input whether punctuation styling was intentionally chosen, omitted, or unavailable.
lenses.why_material: An implementable handoff needs a clear trigger condition for when the optional behavior should activate; otherwise implementation behavior becomes guesswork.
lenses.minimal_test_shape: Present sample requests that include and omit the option, then ask whether the intended output variant is unambiguous in each case.

lenses.failure_description: The synthesized requirements mix abstract rules and sample outputs that do not fully agree, such as examples implying punctuation changes beyond what the written rule allows.
lenses.observable_signal: A reviewer can point to at least one example that cannot be derived directly from the stated requirements.
lenses.why_material: Conflicting synthesized artifacts make the handoff non-implementable because examples and rules compete as sources of truth.
lenses.minimal_test_shape: Check whether every included sample greeting can be explained step-by-step using only the written requirements.

lenses.failure_description: The handoff omits key externally visible decisions such as the default output, supported option values, invalid-input behavior, or whether existing greetings remain unchanged when no option is provided.
lenses.observable_signal: A receiver must invent behavior for at least one common case before writing acceptance criteria or code.
lenses.why_material: Missing decision points force downstream invention, which breaks the goal of producing an implementable requirements handoff.
lenses.minimal_test_shape: Attempt to draft acceptance checks for default case, opted-in case, and invalid option case using only the handoff; note any invented assumptions.

lenses.failure_description: The expected behavior is framed too loosely to support pass-fail evaluation of outputs, especially around formatting differences that are small but user-visible.
lenses.observable_signal: Multiple reviewers disagree on whether a produced greeting is correct because the acceptance target is qualitative rather than exact.
lenses.why_material: Without precise observable outcomes, the handoff cannot reliably confirm whether the requirement was implemented as intended.
lenses.minimal_test_shape: Ask reviewers to judge a small set of candidate outputs against the handoff and measure whether they reach the same verdicts.
